## Ornithology Week 6 Practice Problems: Vocalizations and the Annual Cycle

1) Describe how amplitude, frequency, and time are portrayed on a sonogram. 

2) Harmonics are the result of multiple sound-producing regions in the syrnix operating simultaneously (**T**, **F**, or **It Depends**)  

3) Natural selection on foraging traits such as bill size can influence the frequency of a call through post-source modulation (**T**, **F**, or **It Depends**)  

4) Which of the following correctly describes the acoustic adaptation hypothesis?

    a) selection for communication efficacy leads to birds that live in denser habitats having higher-pitched calls
    b) selection for communication efficacy leads to birds that live in more open habitats having higher-pitched calls
    c) birds with larger body sizes have higher-pitched calls
    d) birds with smaller body sizes have higher-pitched calls

5) Which of the following taxa are vocal learners? (You may circle more than one answer)

    a) passerines
    b) whales
    c) bats
    d) humans

6) What are the four major life cycle events (or "tasks") for migratory birds?

7) Define zeitgeber.

8) Describe experimental evidence (real or hypothetical) for why intrinsic circadian rhythms are imperfect. 

9) Which of the following influence the life cycle stage of a migratory bird?

    a) photoperiod
    b) pineal gland
    c) nesting success or failure
    d) weather
